## What changed from V6

V6 was refused at stage 5 on one root key its closed contract does not declare: one observed event, from which no rate is established. V7 changes the request in one place: the forced tool is strict, and its input schema is the provider-strict projection of schema v1.2.0, frozen by CI gate 92 and pushed as 57154af before any V7 artifact existed. The projection keeps every property name, every required list, every type and enum, the uuid format, and every object closed with additionalProperties false; it sends none of the 30 constraints it classifies LOCAL_ONLY (lengths, counts and three patterns), and each of those is still enforced by the full schema at local stage 5. The output mechanism is FORCED_STRICT_TOOL_USE: tool_choice still forces the one synthesis tool, and the tool definition carries strict: true at its top level, beside its name, description and input schema, with no beta header. Strict decoding is what the provider does while generating; it is not a validation stage, and PROVIDER_STRICT_SUBSET_COMPLIANCE is not FULL_CANONICAL_SCHEMA_COMPLIANCE, which remains LOCAL_STAGE_5_ONLY. The provider documents that a refusal or a max_tokens stop may not match the schema, and stage 3 reads the stop reason before any parse.

The request body, rebuilt through both runners over the same snapshot, differs from V6's in exactly these places: `tools[0].input_schema: changed`; `tools[0].strict: added`. V6's body: 31967 characters; V7's: 31326 (-641). Unchanged: `model`, `max_tokens`, `system`, `messages`, `thinking`, `tool_choice`, `tools[0].name`, `tools[0].description`.
